notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). This package is model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is the deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 model with run_id ros-wave-c-140, reviewed_by stays null; no human reviewed or tested anything, no hardware was attached, and no MuJoCo engine, ROS graph, Gazebo simulator or robot run is claimed.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names helper RosDriver (family ros), but its own candidate classes are cap.world.reset.v1, cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1, its models list is a set of MJCF scenes, and its mock strategy prefers the upstream simulator. The clone's ROS 1 side is a Gazebo runtime with joint command/state topics (unitree_guide, unitree_controller, unitree_legged_control), not a world reset/step service owned by this clone, and it has no Python environment object. This package therefore serves the card's B2 MJCF scene through MujocoDriver; the production path would be the official MuJoCo engine loading the same read-only file. The H1 and G1 scenes and the robot-only XMLs listed by the card are NOT COVERED. The ROS 1 graph, unitree_guide, the joint-command topics, Gazebo, mapping, navigation and SLAM are NOT COVERED, and no ROS endpoint/type is declared.

WHAT IT SERVES: cap.world.step.v1 {ticks, action:{ctrl:[12 numbers]}} writes data.ctrl after the bridge checks each element against the model's actuator_ctrlrange, then runs mj_step per tick; cap.world.reset.v1 runs mj_resetData + mj_forward. The served scene is src/unitree_ros/robots/b2_description_mujoco/xml/scene.xml (includes b2.xml); the B2 model has one free base joint and twelve hinge leg joints, giving 19 qpos and 18 qvel entries, and twelve motor actuators, giving 12 ctrl entries. The ctrlranges are -200..200 for hip and thigh motors and -300..300 for calf motors (b2.xml:170-182); the driver declares no separate Limit and invents no bound. World state = time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed and native_checkpoint. cap.world.seed.v1 is not served by MujocoBridge; reset's seed input is accepted as class metadata but mj_resetData does not use it. The scene declares no <option> timestep; the 2 ms value shown by the fake/reference is the stand-in's placeholder step (and the MuJoCo library default), not a number sourced from the clone.

SAFETY: risk R0 reflects isolated simulated world stepping (MHS/spec/04-safety.md R0, "isolated simulation stepping"); the package exposes no physical mobile-base, actuator-torque or sensor command. The runtime's software e-stop latch blocks step and reset until mhs.safety.reset, while the integration state remains readable; this is not a hardware e-stop and makes no physical-safety claim. No estop_physical_ref is claimed.

FAKE: the fake backend is a package-local stand-in for the mujoco module, not the upstream simulator and not a recording; it replays no captured traffic. It parses the same MJCF scene and its include for the joint shape, the twelve actuator names and ctrlranges, and the option timestep, but loads no mesh, texture or inertia, resolves no contact, friction, tendon, equality or actuator-force constraint, and uses the bridge's basic snapshot profile (time, qpos, qvel, act and ctrl; no full integration/warm-start state). Its F0 timing is lockstep with no wall-clock pacing and a placeholder 2 ms step; the real sim backend would be the official mujoco module loading the same file, which was not installed or run. G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND are the SDK's simulator-family warnings for a class-object backend; they do not mean fake.py is the upstream simulator and no native-call recording is claimed. G8.NO_UNIT x3 are expected for the derived ticks, action.ctrl and seed integer inputs (MHS/handoff/PLAYBOOK.md section 8). No G4.REF_VALUE, G4.REF_BINARY or other G4 warning was raised. G1 passed, so the clone stayed unmodified.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps mhs.testing.check_driver and adds seven cases: model shape from the MJCF (19 qpos, 18 qvel, 12 ctrl, derived -200/-300 ctrlranges), step applying ctrl and advancing ticks/state with the worldbody-vs-actuator order checked, reset restoring the model defaults, malformed inputs rejected before state change, out-of-envelope ctrl refused before state change, e-stop latching step with state readable and reset releasing it, and repeatability of the placeholder state hash. All seven pass; G9 passed.

No catalogue_requests: only catalogue classes cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 are used. No network, pip install, hardware backend, upstream execution or ROS/Gazebo launch was used.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the MujocoDriver deviation (the card's models and world.* candidates are the vendored Unitree MJCF scenes; the clone's ROS 1 side is unitree_guide in Gazebo with joint-command topics and no world service), all twelve facts against the B2 scene, b2.xml and the READMEs, the ctrlrange-derived envelope (b2.xml:170-182, twelve bounded motors), the lockstep latch and the stand-in. The stand-in copied each torque command into its joint velocity and reset qpos to zeros, a zero free-joint quaternion with the base at 0 m, although MuJoCo's qpos0 puts base_link at 0 0 0.8 with the identity quaternion, and a test asserted that zero reset; two facts added claims about the package to their lines (sensors, keyframe). The reviewer changed fake.py (qpos0 parsed from the MJCF, a torque-like placeholder integration), test_driver.py (the reset case expects qpos0, the step case the torque-like response), driver.py (the two facts narrowed; facts on unitree_guide's Go1/A1 and REAL_ROBOT build switch and on the unitree_ros BSD-3 licence; fake and scope gaps; docstring) and facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate and collect.py --strict pass with the MuJoCo-family warnings (G6.NOT_RECORDED, G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND, G8.NO_UNIT x3) and the digest unchanged (sha256:742d27e164e3ba27d2d91319a69f9db864b98ca74b740055a9f0fb1ae8dd37f7); the author's notes on the zero reset and the joint-velocity placeholder are superseded. The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence not stated (NOASSERTION)); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it. For the human reviewer: Simulation only: the bare B2 MuJoCo plant (twelve torque motors, no controller), so after reset the robot falls from 0.8 m unless a caller supplies torques; the keyframe home is not applied. The repository's primary runtime, unitree_guide with Go1 or A1 in Gazebo, can be compiled for a real robot (REAL_ROBOT, CMakeLists.txt:4-9, 87-95) and is NOT COVERED. Licence: unitree_ros is BSD-3-Clause (Unitree); the repository has no root licence.
